title: Divide and recombine approaches for fitting logistic regression to large-scale health surveillance data: application to diabetes risk prediction in BRFSS
target_definition: Published text: DIABETE4; gestational excluded; prediabetes grouped as non-diabetic
feature_strategy: Literature-grounded; consistent annual availability; <20% missing each year; pairwise correlation <0.7
models_or_method: Logistic regression; D&R vs glm and speedglm
validation_and_imbalance: Complete-case primary analysis; multiple-imputation sensitivity; computational partition sensitivity
how_we_use_it: Feature-selection criteria; target-operationalization comparison; large-scale BRFSS precedent
cautions: Public R script currently maps DIABETE4 1=Yes and 3=No and drops other categories, which appears inconsistent with published statement that prediabetes is non-diabetic; reproduce and resolve before adopting

title: Building Risk Prediction Models for Type 2 Diabetes Using Machine Learning Techniques
target_definition: Age >30; yes to diabetes; pregnant diabetes and prediabetes excluded
feature_strategy: 27 variables selected from diabetes-risk literature; complete cases
models_or_method: SVM variants; Gaussian NB; Logistic Regression; Neural Network; Decision Tree; Random Forest
validation_and_imbalance: 2/3 train, 1/3 untouched test; SMOTE applied to training only; accuracy/sensitivity/specificity/AUC
public_code: No public code located; full CDC article and variable appendix
how_we_use_it: Raw-BRFSS feature precedent; target definition; leakage-safe train-only SMOTE; benchmark design
cautions: Older BRFSS coding (DIABETE3); holdout rather than modern nested/CV workflow

title: Exploring Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting and Interpreting Self-Reported Diabetes among Tennessee Adults: Insights from the 2023 BRFSS
venue: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health
feature_strategy: EDA + bivariate screening + backward elimination + Cramer's V + RFE
models_or_method: Logistic Regression; SVM; KNN; Decision Tree; Random Forest; Gradient Boosting; XGBoost; SHAP
validation_and_imbalance: 80/20 stratified split; SMOTE on training only; stratified 5-fold CV within train; accuracy/precision/recall/balanced accuracy/F1/AUROC/PR-AUC
public_code: No public code located; detailed methods and supplemental hyperparameter/feature tables
how_we_use_it: Closest methodological template for our class benchmark; metrics; CV; SHAP; self-reported-status wording
cautions: State-specific sample rather than national; mixed R/Stata/Python pipeline

title: An investigation of machine learning algorithms and data augmentation techniques for diabetes diagnosis using class imbalanced BRFSS dataset
feature_strategy: Health and socioeconomic predictors; emphasis on end-to-end imbalance handling
models_or_method: Multiple ML algorithms with SMOTE-N, ENN, SMOTE-Tomek, SMOTE-ENN
validation_and_imbalance: Sampling applied to training data to avoid leakage
public_code: No public repository located; article methods are detailed; data stated public at CDC
how_we_use_it: Imbalance protocol and leakage-safe resampling reference
cautions: Exact annual-file/provenance and full reconstruction details should be checked before numerical comparison

title: Diabetes prediction model based on GA-XGBoost and stacking ensemble algorithm
sample_or_scope: 438,693 raw records; 303 variables; authors select 25 features
feature_strategy: 25 selected features; preprocessing; GA-XGBoost feature/model optimization
models_or_method: Decision Tree; Logistic Regression; AdaBoost; LightGBM; XGBoost; GA-XGBoost; stacking; SHAP
validation_and_imbalance: Compares ROS, ADASYN, SMOTE, SMOTEENN; reports standard classification metrics
public_code: No public code located; public input dataset and detailed paper workflow
how_we_use_it: Modern raw-year BRFSS comparison; boosting/SHAP; feature shortlist cross-check

title: A copula based supervised filter for feature selection in machine learning driven diabetes risk prediction
brfss_basis: UCI CDC Diabetes Health Indicators derived from BRFSS 2015
feature_strategy: Copula upper-tail-dependence feature ranking benchmarked against MI, mRMR, ReliefF, L1/Elastic-Net
models_or_method: Four classifiers; feature-selection benchmarking; statistical tests and robustness checks
validation_and_imbalance: Train/test workflow in public Python implementation; reproducible UCI fetch via ucimlrepo
how_we_use_it: Reproducible feature-selection reference; candidate-variable evidence; code pattern
cautions: Uses curated BRFSS-2015 derivative and conflates prediabetes with diabetes; not directly comparable to our DIABETE4 binary target

title: An assessment of machine learning models and algorithms for early prediction and diagnosis of diabetes using health indicators
sample_or_scope: 253,680 unbalanced records / 21 indicators; also discusses balanced subset
target_definition: Diabetes_binary in curated dataset; prediabetes/diabetes combined in positive class
feature_strategy: EDA/PCA highlights BMI, age, BP, cholesterol, general health, physical health, walking difficulty, income
models_or_method: Decision Tree; Random Forest; KNN; Naive Bayes; Logistic Regression
validation_and_imbalance: Multiple classification metrics including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, ROC-AUC and PR curves
public_code: No public code located; detailed appendix and model settings
how_we_use_it: Established 21-indicator benchmark and common baseline algorithms

title: AI-driven analysis of diabetes risk determinants in U.S. adults: Exploring disease prevalence and health factors
target_definition: Diabetes/prediabetes prevalence reported around 14% in analytical sample
feature_strategy: Broad health/social determinant features; supplementary coding file and correlation matrix
models_or_method: 18 classifiers including LR, RF, Extra Trees, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost; SHAP

how_we_use_it: Broad model catalogue; SHAP; feature-importance comparison
cautions: Data-availability statement points to raw CDC 2015 (~441k) while analytical sample is 253,680, indicating provenance ambiguity; reported AUC near 0.99 merits independent replication

title: An interpretable machine learning approach to predicting depression and diabetes
target_definition: Diabetes outcome alongside separate depression outcome
feature_strategy: Behavioral, demographic and socioeconomic features; interpretable ML
models_or_method: Multiple ML algorithms with SHAP-style interpretability
validation_and_imbalance: Multi-year BRFSS comparison; article describes model benchmarking

title: Detecting High-Risk Factors and Early Diagnosis of Diabetes Using Machine Learning Methods
